column1: # Token families that denote one operation but that the two languages spell
# differently.  Column 1 is the canonical spelling both sides compare as; column 2 is
# the comma-separated family; column 3 records why the family is legitimate.
# A family does two things: every body check canonicalises it to column 1, and the
# family gets an occurrence check (the port must use it at least as often as the C body
# does).  The occurrence check is not optional: a note that merely allowed `memcpy` to
# be absent let a body with all three of doprnt's output copies deleted pass both

column3: std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping is the port's memcpy/mempcpy; gnulib's rpl_mempcpy keeps its C name
Rust spells C's va_arg macro as VaList::next_arg
gnulib's ckd_add stores the wrapped sum and reports overflow; Rust's overflowing_add is that pair (P-15)
C's `sizeof` is Rust's `size_of::<T> ()`; the family's occurrence check then requires the port to spell it as often as the C body does

C's `local_if_set` bitfield (lisp.h 3080) is the mirror's `BLV_LOCAL_IF_SET` flag inside `u.s.bits` (lisp.rs 1971); the occurrence check is what makes `make_blv`'s clear (data.c 2170) and `set_internal`'s read (data.c 1766) survive a deletion, which the note-based exemption could not (review B's D1, P-78 residual 4)
